title: Quote, valuation ratios, ratings and 52-week range for NASDAQ:AMAL (Amalgamated Financial Corp.) silently show the unrelated Indian BSE 506597 'Amal Ltd' chemicals maker's real data
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/quotes/AMAL?asset_class=equity and GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/AMAL and GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/AMAL/ratings, with no region override, while this battery slot is explicitly NASDAQ:AMAL. All three return the Indian bulk-chemicals maker Amal Ltd's real, current numbers as a flat 200: price 720.8 INR (not $47.40), market_cap INR 891cr (not $1.42B), pe_ratio 29.98 (not 12.64), price_to_book 7.40 (not 1.70), eps 24.04 INR (not $3.75), fifty_two_week_high/low 1010.0/408.2 (not 51.59/25.13), name 'Amal Ltd', sector 'Basic Materials'/'Chemicals' (not 'Financials'/'Banks - Regional') — with fundamentals.identity_note = null, i.e. no disclosed disagreement of any kind.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P19_AMAL.json (calls.quote.body, calls.fundamentals.body, calls.ratings.body — name 'Amal Ltd'/'AMAL.BO', currency INR) vs docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P19_AMAL.json (identity.legal_name, price.last_close, market_cap, pe_ttm, pb, week52); collected.calls.resolve_bare_symbol.body — candidates carry BOTH 'Amal Ltd' (BSE, region IN, confidence 1.0) and 'Amalgamated Financial Corp.' (US, region US, confidence 1.0) yet needs_disambiguation=false and resolved binds to BSE; sidecar/services/provider_registry.py:288-302 (_effective_region: an ambiguous bare ticker with no unambiguous master hint falls through to config.get_region(), the request-default region, not to any per-symbol disambiguation); sidecar/services/resolution_policy.py:26-35 ('A cross-region tie is NOT residual: region is the separating evidence ... so the bind stands' — D58b, documented deliberate policy); sidecar/routers/quotes.py:52-53 (get_quote(symbol, asset_class) — no region parameter exposed at all) and sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:88-89 (get_fundamentals(symbol) — same; only get_company_narrative at :153-160 takes an X-Vysted-Region header); sidecar/routers/fundamentals.py:54-82 (_identity_note re-resolves the SAME symbol via the SAME region-defaulted policy that produced the wrong bind in the first place, so it structurally cannot catch this class of error — it can only catch provider-vs-resolver disagreement on an already-correct bind).
notes: Root cause: an intentional, documented resolver policy (D58b) that a same-symbol cross-region tie binds silently by locale rank, combined with zero of the actual data routes (/quotes, /fundamentals, /fundamentals/.../ratings) accepting a region/exchange qualifier to override that default. The consequence is exactly the failure the product's 'data trust' moat exists to prevent: a user who has ALREADY correctly identified NASDAQ:AMAL (e.g. via chat @-mention using the full company name, which DOES resolve correctly per collected.calls.resolve_company_name) gets a completely different, real, plausible-looking company's price/ratios/52-week range the moment they open the equity-overview panel for the bare ticker, with no badge, no warning, no identity_note — wrong money-relevant data shown as true. Smallest fix shape: thread the already-resolved instrument's region/exchange from /resolve (or the chat mention binding) through to /quotes/{symbol}, /fundamentals/{symbol} and /fundamentals/{symbol}/ratings as an optional region/exchange query param (the plumbing already exists one layer down — provider_registry.get_quote/get_fundamentals already accept a region kwarg; only the router layer drops it) so a panel that already knows which AMAL the user means does not have to silently re-guess.

title: India-only shareholding and announcements endpoints silently serve a different, real company's data for a US-collision ticker with no region guard or error
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/shareholding?symbol=AMAL and GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/announcements?symbol=AMAL&limit=25 for the NASDAQ:AMAL slot both return a flat 200 with Amal Ltd's (BSE 506597) real, current BSE-filed shareholding pattern (promoter 71.35%, dii 0.03%, quarter 2026-06-30) and its real AGM announcement, with no field, flag or error indicating these routes cannot serve the US company at all.
evidence: sidecar/routers/disclosures.py:44-46 (get_announcements docstring/param: 'symbol: NSE/BSE ticker' — an India-only route by design) and :95-97 (get_shareholding: same, 'symbol: NSE ticker') — neither takes a region/exchange param and neither validates that the resolved instrument is actually Indian before answering; docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P19_AMAL.json calls.shareholding.body (promoter_percent 71.35, source 'BSE') and calls.announcements.body (1 BSE AGM filing) — both real, well-formed, wrong-company answers for a slot whose intended instrument (per docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/manifest.json P19 entry) is NASDAQ:AMAL.
notes: Distinct from DAT-P19-1: these two routes are structurally India-only (their own docstrings say so), so for the US entity the CORRECT app behaviour is an honest 'not applicable to a non-Indian instrument' response — pack.shareholding explicitly marks promoter/fii/dii/pledge as structurally_absent for a US issuer, not merely undisclosed. Instead the endpoints happily answer with a real, wrong company's real, gameable numbers (promoter holding is explicitly the single most gameable Indian small-cap figure per the pack), indistinguishable from a genuine answer. Smallest fix shape: corporate_disclosures.get_shareholding/get_announcements should reject (or clearly flag) a symbol whose resolved instrument's exchange/region is not NSE/BSE, rather than resolving the bare string and serving whatever the BSE master happens to contain for it.

title: Results-calendar route hard-502s for the actively-traded NASDAQ:AMAL with a misleading 'not a known NSE instrument' error, instead of degrading honestly
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/disclosures/results?symbol=AMAL returns HTTP 502 {"detail": "nse_direct: 'AMAL' is not a known NSE instrument"} for a stock that trades daily on Nasdaq with a real, published next-earnings date (2026-10-22).
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P19_AMAL.json calls.results_calendar (status 502, detail as above); sidecar/routers/disclosures.py:74-76 (get_results: 'symbol: NSE ticker' — India-only by design, same pattern as DAT-P19-2's endpoints) propagating a ProviderError as a raw 502 rather than an honest empty/not-applicable 200; outside truth docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P19_AMAL.json latest_results.next_earnings_date (2026-10-22, https://stockanalysis.com/stocks/amal/statistics/).
notes: The mandatory latest_results field (quarter/filing_date/next_earnings_date) is completely unreachable for this slot: not a labelled gap, a hard error. The message itself is also misleading — 'AMAL is not a known NSE instrument' reads as 'this ticker does not exist', when in fact it is a well-known, actively-traded NASDAQ stock; a user hitting this would reasonably conclude the app has no idea what AMAL is at all, rather than 'this results calendar only covers Indian exchanges'. Smallest fix shape: catch the region mismatch before it reaches nse_direct and return a 200 with an honest 'results calendar not available for non-NSE instruments' reason, mirroring the pattern the R13 identity_note / field_meta machinery already uses elsewhere in this same codebase.

title: No field anywhere carries declared/record/ex/payable dividend dates or any corporate-action (split/bonus/buyback/AGM) history, for either the mandatory dividend sub-fields or corporate_actions_2026
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/AMAL returns dividend_per_share and dividend_yield but no declared/record/ex/payable date for either; grep of sidecar/routers/ finds no route anywhere (India or US) that serves splits, bonus, rights, buyback authorizations or AGM results.
evidence: sidecar/models/fundamentals.py:73-74 (dividend_per_share field, no accompanying date fields anywhere in the class) and :106-111 (dividend_per_share_ttm docstring explicitly frames the declared-vs-paid distinction yet the field is left null for this slot — see the diff's dividend.paid_trailing_12m_per_share row); grep of sidecar/routers/ (quotes.py, fundamentals.py, disclosures.py) confirms no corporate-action/buyback/AGM endpoint exists for any region; outside truth docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P19_AMAL.json dividend.last_declared_per_share (record/ex/payable dates, all filed) and corporate_actions_2026 (buyback, AGM, dividend history).
notes: Same underlying schema gap already raised for the Indian half of this collision (DAT-P9-3), confirmed independently here for the US instrument — this is not region-specific, it is a structural absence for every symbol the app serves. The DIFF spec marks both the declared-vs-paid dividend distinction and corporate_actions_2026 as mandatory fields; both fail here for a reason unrelated to the entity-resolution bug in DAT-P19-1/2, i.e. even a correctly resolved AMAL would still be missing these. Smallest fix shape: add a corporate-actions sub-resource (dividend record/ex/pay dates, splits, buybacks, AGM outcomes) sourced from the same SEC/BSE filing feeds the pack itself used, and populate dividend_per_share_ttm from it.

title: 52-week high/low as-of dates carry only the API fetch timestamp, never the date the high/low actually occurred
repro: GET http://127.0.0.1:52152/fundamentals/AMAL returns field_meta.fifty_two_week_high.as_of and field_meta.fifty_two_week_low.as_of both equal to '2026-09-19T10:00:06.979185+00:00' — the moment the call ran, not 2026-08-13 (the pack's verified date of the true 52w high) or any other date the extreme actually printed.
evidence: docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/collected/P19_AMAL.json calls.fundamentals.body.field_meta.fifty_two_week_high / .fifty_two_week_low (as_of identical to every other field's fetch timestamp, e.g. market_cap's as_of); sidecar/models/fundamentals.py FieldMeta usage — as_of is populated uniformly per-fetch, with no per-value event-date concept for these two fields specifically; outside truth docs/redesign/verification/r15/battery/packs/P19_AMAL.json week52.high.date (2026-08-13) / week52.low.date (2025-10-16), each independently corroborated by a second source.
notes: Mandatory subtle-tier requirement per the DIFF spec ('a 52w high/low pair is often stale in one leg and fresh in the other' / 'diff the as-of date too'). Independent of the wrong-entity bug in DAT-P19-1 — even a correctly resolved AMAL would have this same gap, since field_meta's as_of is a fetch-time stamp by construction, not an event-time stamp. As the pack's own traps note for this exact kind of field ('all_time_high_is_stale_not_wrong'), a cached extremum without its own as_of silently rots into a lie over time with no source ever having been wrong. Smallest fix shape: carry the actual high/low print date alongside the value (most providers, including yfinance's own daily-bar series, already expose it) rather than only the API-call timestamp.
